title: Supreme Court Refuses to Interfere With Delhi HC Restraint on 'Saurashtra Aaj Tak' Newspaper Name
case_name: Saurashtra Aaj Tak v. TV Today Network Limited
card_summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a Gujarati newspaper's challenge to a Delhi HC order restraining use of the name 'Saurashtra Aaj Tak'. It held TV Today Network, which runs the channel Aaj Tak, the prior user, and called the case one of clear passing off. The newspaper had kept the title since 2002 under a trial order allowing a disclaimer, set aside by the High Court in July 2026. It gets three months to drop the name.
card_tip: A disclaimer does not cure deceptive similarity to a well-known mark; prior use, not how long or how regionally a name has been used, decides a passing-off claim.
verification_notes: Decision date (7 Oct 2026) and core holding (passing off, prior user, three-month rebranding window) confirmed across Verdictum, Exchange4Media and LawChakra. Bench composition (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Bagchi and Mohana) and underlying Delhi HC judgment date (30 July 2026) consistent across sources, except one report named the third judge 'V. Mahadevan' instead of 'V. Mohana'; used the more frequently reported spelling.
